status: OPEN: controlled startup defect corrected; exact natural-stall attribution remains unproven
correction: Eight launcher lines check pending owner-task cancellation before online announcement and again after its awaited kernel enqueue. Interrupted startup propagates cancellation through existing cleanup without granting orderly checkpoint intent.

controlled_windows_red.failure_cases: Consumed cancellation at core-load or announcement, with ordinary or marked CLI SIGINT delivery, entered the operation loop and failed to reach owned cleanup.

controlled_windows_green.selection: Nine new startup cases plus existing launcher shutdown and Windows SIGINT controls. Normal boot/orderly SIGINT retains checkpoint intent; cancelled startup records only save_checkpoint=False.
controlled_windows_green.genuine_wait_for_case: Uses a real completed Future and actual cancellation. Windows 3.13 propagates it; Linux 3.11 can consume it, as separately reproduced in the Homeostasis receipt.

awaited_task_diagnostics.proof: A real parent awaits a boot Task placed beyond the initial 32 roots; capture follows the read-only guarded Task edge, retaining numeric links and cancellation count. Deep-chain/dedup tests retain global bounds and privacy.

limits: The natural strict/full captures identify a test awaiting its cancelled launcher task, but omit that task own await chain. The controlled defect does not prove that missing chain or historical common cause.
No runtime authority, Guardian/Security, signing or checkpoint approval boundary changes. Tests simulate marked SIGINT; these are not new physical keyboard checks.
Final exact-head Linux results must be checked on PR #387.
